clue.text: The Queen's in Woking to meet 100 girls who wear blue collars

indicators.note: the Queen sitting in the town means her letter goes inside the town's name

parts.note: the Surrey commuter town, taken as written
R for Regina, the Latin for queen
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: The Queen visits a Surrey town to meet a crowd of factory girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Woking is a commuter town in Surrey. R goes inside it, then C and LASSES follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-collar workers are manual labourers, the traditional membership of the working classes as opposed to office staff.

clue.text: See water crocus, perhaps, mixed with tomato juice

definitions.note: describes the answer by what it is added to, rather than naming it

indicators.note: perhaps says these letters could become something else if arranged differently

explanation.surface: A garden scene of a crocus by water, oddly blended into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' looks like the anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition; 'perhaps' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The spicy condiment is a classic ingredient added to a Bloody Mary cocktail alongside vodka and tomato.

clue.text: This unpleasant place could be real hot

indicators.note: could be invites the solver to turn these letters into another possible word

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a grim place could get uncomfortably hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rathole is a squalid, filthy room or building, slang for any wretched and dirty lodging.

clue.text: Briefly smashing in new door

indicators.note: smashing breaks the words apart so the pieces can be rebuilt differently

explanation.surface: A quick report of a burglar breaking through a newly fitted door.
explanation.definitionFit: Summing something up concisely or in short is saying it in a single term, so both mean concisely put.

clue.text: The writing's on the wall for Steffi before match one

parts.note: Steffi Graf, the German tennis champion
to fit is to match or suit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tennis star facing defeat before her first match: the writing is on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles; her surname supplies the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is literally scrawled lettering on walls, so the idiom about doom is reread as a plain description.

clue.text: Made-up story (vulgar), so keep out of sight

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: Someone who told a crude fib had better hide for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is an idiom for staying hidden and avoiding attention until trouble passes.

clue.text: Thus Nick nearly makes a sort of boom

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective in the phrase sonic boom

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all of the name, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A man named Nick almost causes some kind of explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonic boom is the loud bang produced when an aircraft breaks the sound barrier, so the word names that kind.

clue.text: Look at you once, turning up with a mutilated label

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the old pronoun from bottom to top

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of you

indicators.note: a mutilated thing is damaged out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone eyes you up after spotting a torn label on your clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is informal for staring at them hard, a slangy synonym for looking.

clue.text: "Leg up", I cry later around place where works of art are found

definitions.text: place where works of art are found

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a boost over a wall and complains afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture gallery is a room or building displaying paintings, the kind of museum space that houses artworks.

clue.text: Fundamental reason for helping to get the beer

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: The real reason for lending a hand is to be rewarded with a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' reads as assisting, but it is a noun: a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying logic or justification behind an action or belief.

clue.text: Donna evidently displays birthmarks

indicators.note: displays means the run of letters is shown within the words

explanation.surface: A woman called Donna clearly has marks on her skin from birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi is the medical plural of naevus, a congenital mole or pigmented patch on the skin.

clue.text: Ant leaves antelope to run off

indicators.note: leaves means the insect's name departs from the animal's name

explanation.surface: A tiny ant climbs off a grazing antelope and scurries away.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly, especially in order to marry without consent.

clue.text: Amorous man returns to talk about right operational sequence

indicators.note: returns means the predatory man's name goes back the way it came

parts.note: a wolf is a predatory womaniser

indicators.note: about means the talk wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A ladies' man comes back to discuss the right way to do things.
explanation.definitionFit: A flow chart is a diagram showing the steps of a process in order, mapping a procedure step by step.

clue.text: Dixie, where the silence holds out

indicators.note: holds means the call for quiet keeps the other word inside it

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A Southern state where a code of silence keeps outsiders out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie is the nickname for the states of the American South, the former Confederacy.

clue.text: … or let's out the man working in the stable

definitions.text: the man working in the stable

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: Continuing a thought: or let's call out the stable hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostler was the groom at an inn who looked after travellers' horses.

clue.text: Reconstruct the bricks to make a place for an invalid

indicators.note: to reconstruct is to rebuild in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Builders reuse old bricks to put up a home for someone unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A sick berth is the ship's sickbay, the bunks where ailing sailors are treated on board.

clue.text: Unused port in excess

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
over means too much or in excess

explanation.surface: Too much port has been bought, and some was never drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftover food or material is what remains surplus after the rest has been consumed.

clue.text: Married, getting externally harsh medicine

indicators.note: getting something on the outside means a word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: a reedy voice is thin and harsh
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A newlywed is handed a bitter dose of medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment or cure for illness, a synonym for a drug or medicine.

clue.text: Cleaver cuts me with each try

indicators.note: cuts means the following words slice into the pronoun

parts.note: ea is the abbreviation for each
to tax is to try or strain, as in taxing patience

explanation.surface: A butcher's blade slices into the speaker at every attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy chopping knife for butchery, also called a meat-axe.

clue.text: Getting to call everyone inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for everyone sits within the other

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: Phoning everyone in turn to get through to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a place or person means arriving at or contacting it, which is what getting to means.

clue.text: "One gains no good when keeping slim" (Vogue)

indicators.note: keeping means the outer letters hold the word for slim within them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for no, as on a yes/no form
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A fashion magazine's warning that dieting brings no benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vogue' in brackets looks like crediting the magazine, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in vogue is fashionable, and the in-thing is the currently fashionable craze.

clue.text: Authority for Henry in February to go North

definitions.note: a noun used in 'on behalf of', meaning on the authority of

indicators.note: in means the king's name is placed inside the month
in a down clue, going north means reading the month upwards

parts.note: Hal is a nickname for Henry, as with Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A permit lets Henry travel north in February.
explanation.walkthrough: Acting on someone's behalf means acting with their authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on behalf of another means with their mandate or permission, the sense of authority here.

clue.text: Pictures kept by blokes in suitable dwelling-place

indicators.note: in means the paired words sit inside the word for suitable

explanation.surface: Some men keep paintings in a fitting home.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms used as a residence or home.

clue.text: Coupon given to Kenneth

parts.note: Ken is short for Kenneth; the letters also happen to run straight through these two words, a coincidence of the charade

explanation.surface: A voucher is handed to a man called Kenneth.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a voucher exchangeable for goods, like a book token, so it is a kind of coupon.

clue.text: A leaf or nut should be put by the telephone

parts.note: tel is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave a leaf or nut beside the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel is the Asian vine whose leaf is chewed wrapped around the areca nut, also called the betel nut.

clue.text: Eccentric about social position

parts.note: c for circa, Latin for about
rank is one's status in society

explanation.surface: An oddball who is obsessed with class and status.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is an odd person with strange fixed ideas, a noun synonym for an oddball.

clue.text: Plug: it's hostile to hold it back

indicators.note: to hold means the word for hostile keeps the other inside
back means the pronoun is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a stopper is awkward to hold in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a product is informal for promoting or publicising it heavily.

clue.text: November plea from Penelope in support of the chap

explanation.surface: Penelope makes an appeal on behalf of some man.
explanation.walkthrough: On Bonfire Night, 5 November, British children traditionally showed off a stuffed effigy of Guy Fawkes, the guy, and begged passers-by for coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the children's traditional begging cry heard in the run-up to Guy Fawkes Night each autumn.
